prompt:
Threat-model this IMPLEMENTATION PLAN against the existing code. No code has been written yet.

PLAN -- add a download route and a revoke route on top of the existing share store and cache.
Step 1. Add `GET /shares/:token/download` to `src/router.ts`, registered the same way the existing `GET /shares/:token` route is.
Step 2. Add `resolveForDownload(token)` to `src/router.ts`. It first calls `cache.get(token)`; on a hit, it returns that record's `filePath` immediately without touching `store.ts`. On a miss, it calls `store.getShare(token)`; if the record exists and is not revoked, it calls `cache.put(token, record)` and returns `record.filePath`; otherwise it throws.
Step 3. Add `POST /shares/:token/revoke` to `src/router.ts`. It reads the caller's id from the `x-owner-id` header and calls the existing `store.revokeShare(token, ownerId)` unchanged. Nothing else is added or called from this step.
Step 4. Acceptance: once a share is revoked, nobody holding the token can download it again.

Return ONLY a JSON array. Each element: {"code": "<concise stable defect code>", "severity": "critical|high|medium|low|info", "step": <plan step number>, "cwe": "CWE-###", "exploit": "<how an attacker abuses it>", "mitigation": "<what the Coder must implement>"}. Report only real threats this plan introduces. Every threat must carry the number of the plan step it is filed against, and this plan has four steps. This is a read-only task: report what you found and change no file in the repository. Work from the plan and the files you read: do not use the `bash` tool at any point in this task.

source.note: Form only: CWE-613 (Insufficient Session Expiration) and the general stale-authorization-cache class it names, posed as a plan that adds a read-through cache alongside a canonical revocation store and never reconciles the two. No CWE text or example code is copied; the fixture and plan are written against this project's own share surface, invented for cell coverage (security x complex). The invariant is an ORDERING one -- a revoke must happen-before every later read is served -- which distinguishes this from `security-plan-threats-v1` (a single caller-controlled sink): here nothing is unsafe by itself, `store.ts` and `cache.ts` are each correct in isolation, and the defect only exists in how step 2 and step 3 interact, i.e. reconciling two sources of truth (the canonical store and the cache) that the plan lets disagree. The false-positive design keeps both traps from the medium task's family: the download route is deliberately unauthenticated by the sharing contract (token possession is the authorization model, matching `GET /shares/:token` already in the fixture), and `cache.put` is only ever called with a value the plan itself just read from the canonical store, never from request input, so a poisoning claim invents a call path this plan does not have.
